ios.desc:
For Art’s Sake – Your Daily Art History Companion

Discover the stories behind the world’s greatest masterpieces—right on your device. For Art’s Sake turns every morning into an inspiring lesson in art history, guiding you from Renaissance frescoes and Baroque brilliance to Pre-Raphaelite dreams and Impressionist light.

Why For Art’s Sake?
•	Daily Art Discovery – one museum-quality insight served fresh every day
•	200+ High-Res Masterpieces – download stellar images for study or wallpapers
•	35+ Artists & 10+ Movements – comprehensive art history coverage in your pocket
•	Expert-Curated Learning – quizzes, spotlights & deep-dives by real art historians
•	Personalized Journey – save favorites, build collections and set widgets or wallpapers

Key Features (Free)

Art of the Day
•	One iconic painting delivered each morning
•	Rich description, historical context and ultra-high-resolution image
•	Focus on key works from early Renaissance to Pre-Raphaelite visionaries

Library of Favorites
•	Save and revisit beloved artworks, artists or movements
•	Build custom collections of museum-quality images and deep-dive articles

Art of the Day Widget
•	New masterpiece on your Home Screen every day
•	Tap to unlock full background, artist bio and cultural impact

Search & Filter
•	Instantly locate any artist, artwork or movement in our curated database
•	Filter by era, style, technique or curator picks

For Art’s Sake Pro (Auto-Renewable Subscription)

Unlock premium content curated by our historians:
Gallery Spotlight (Pro)
•	Weekly highlight of treasures from world-class museums (The National Gallery, the Louvre, Museo del Prado, etc.)
•	Curator commentary plus links for virtual gallery tours

High-Res Downloads & Wallpapers (Pro)
•	One-tap save of ultra-high-resolution images
•	Set legendary works as wallpapers or lock-screen art

Monthly Spotlight Collections (Pro)
•	12 seasonal themes—Renaissance in January to Winter Glow in December
•	In-depth analysis and curator notes for each chosen masterpiece

Daily Quizzes (Pro)
•	Fast, engaging quizzes on artists, movements and individual works
•	Instant feedback so you can track your growing art history knowledge

Art Movements Explorer (Pro)
•	Explore 10+ major movements, from Renaissance and Baroque to Impressionism and Cubism
•	Learn defining traits, pivotal works and lasting cultural impact

Artist Profiles & Deep Dives (Pro)
•	35+ detailed artist bios—Turner, Goya, Monet, van Gogh and beyond
•	Signature works, memorabl

quotes.text:
My collection of art, philosophy and poetry apps. They have previously just been on iOS but I just finished the Kotlin port of the art one, so will be releasing that soon.

The poetry one is react native. Art and philosophy ones are swift/kotlin. I wanted to see if you could use LLMs to effectively create a cross-platform app. The idea behind react native was that you write it once in an approachable language, then the framework compiles to native app code. In 2025, the approachable language you code in is English, and the LLM now generates native app code.

It was generally a success and I feel less of a need of the development overhead of react native these days.

quotes.text:
I find creating an app around a subject is actually a great way to teach myself about something. I previously had success with a classic poems app then a philosophy app. Art history made sense to do next.
I'm a web dev by trade but used ChatGPT to help me create a native SwiftUI app. Very happy with the look and feel of it. Feedback welcome!
